coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Employment (Domestic Workers) Regulations 2009 (S 39/2009, amended 2014) under Employment Order 2009 Part XII; Labour Department licenses employers recruiting domestic workers and licenses employment agencies (Employment Agencies Order 2004). Nothing new beyond K13/K04; households go through agencies.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: One search; no Brunei scrap-metal dealer licensing regime found (results all other countries). Unverified whether one exists.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Pawnbrokers Order 2002 (S 60/2002): licensing officer, licence required (s.9), record of pawn agreements (s.14), safe-keeping (s.16). No second-hand dealer register found. Licensee count unknown, likely very small. Order text is scanned, unreadable via fetch.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K12 (jewellers AML rejected, too few shops). No separate search spent.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: One search; no Brunei end-of-life vehicle or dismantler regime found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Animal (Diseases and Quarantine) Order 2021 makes the DAA Director the competent veterinary authority and covers animal movement within and into Brunei plus quarantine. Livestock-trader specific record duties not found. Not separately searched.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Wholesome Meat Order 2011 and Wholesome Meat (Slaughtering Centres) Regulations 2011 (licence by Director of BDFA, applicant must be registered business); Halal Meat Act Cap 183 and rules (halal licence, slaughtering centre approval, import permits, Syariah Affairs Halal Food Control Division). Few slaughtering centres; PDFs unreadable. See candidate on slaughtering centres.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No search spent (budget used on higher-regulation categories). Likely nothing regulated.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: 2005 Veterinary Surgeons order with Annual Practising Certificate and a Veterinary Council (per search summary, unconfirmed); DAA is veterinary authority. Handful of private vets; no commercial veterinary-medicine permit process found.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: No search spent (budget). Brunei is piped-water served; low likelihood.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Environmental Protection and Management Order 2016 (JASTRe); MOH tenders require contractors registered with MOH and licensed for domestic waste collection; vehicles approved by JASTRe; Sungai Paku septic sludge facility. No specific desludging licence rule confirmed.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Two searches; no Brunei lift/boiler certification rule or inspectors found (results were Malaysia/HK). Unverified; Labour Department or Ministry of Development is the likely home.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Brunei water supply is a government utility (Water Services Department); no small private water systems expected. Not searched.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: No Brunei pesticides order found; Poisons Act Cap 114 requires a licence from a Licensing Officer to import, possess for sale or sell poisons; Customs Application Permit for poisons and deleterious drugs per WTO notes; Agriculture Department controls restricted agri imports. Unverified whether pesticides sit here.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Labour Department licenses employment agencies for foreign workers (Employment Agencies Order 2004; Foreign Workers Recruitment Licence s.112 Employment Order 2009). Since 2016 Foreign Worker Licence (LPA) replaced the Labour Quota Licence; per business.gov.bn new LPA applications must go through a registered employment agent; mandatory inspection 3-6 months after approval; security deposit; JobCentre Brunei clearance letter. Nothing new beyond K03/K04.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Nothing found on funeral-service licensing; burial is run via religious bodies and district offices. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Societies Act Cap 66 (Registrar of Societies; registration order, Registrar may call for constitution and accounts, ss.11-14). No annual return duty confirmed. Halal supervision falls under K01.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: JPD and Royal Brunei Police enforce Road Traffic Act Cap 68; buses franchised and tendered; taxis franchised; e-hailing unregulated on price. No operator register or periodic report details found.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Money-changers and remittance firms: BDCB licence under Money-Changing and Remittance Businesses Act Cap 174, annual fee BND 2,000 (money-changing) / BND 3,000 plus BND 55,000 guarantee (remittance), mandatory Compliance Officer since 1 May 2020, AML/CFT under Criminal Asset Recovery Order 2012, BDCB opens applications only periodically. Tamu/hawker licensing: nothing found.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: BDFA inspects food premises with scored checklist (70%+ satisfactory; below 51 unsatisfactory with counselling; 50 or less closed immediately) and requires Basic Food Safety Course for all food handlers. Draft Food Order 2024 would replace Public Health (Food) Act Cap 182 and regulate home-based businesses and stalls as food premises; gazettal not confirmed. Child care centres licensed by MCYS (KKBS) with multi-agency review (police record, traffic, fire, health, planning; 2019). Driving schools, tattoo studios, hunting: no data.
